before.prompt: If Gold 2 moves into your new route, what could you do?

options.text: Change direction or stay as another support option
Insist on the return pass anyway

before.explanation: The pass does not obligate the receiver to return it; another support action may be better.

after.prompt: F2 has the puck. YOU want to offer a backward outlet farther from both gold defenders. Which direction should YOU explore first in this view?

options.text: Toward the side boards beside F2

after.explanation: Moving toward Navy’s net offers F2 an option farther back and initially takes YOU farther from both gold defenders. Moving toward Gold’s net closes those gaps; moving toward F2’s side boards brings YOU closer to Gold 1. Check the passing line and F2’s next action. This is one support plan, not a required retreat; a forward or wider option can become useful as pressure changes.

optionReasons.reason: Right-net direction closes both gold gaps; plausible attacking give-and-go but not backward separation.
Positive-y board direction decreases Gold1 gap but increases Gold2 gap; plausible wider support but not both aims.
Left-net direction increases both gold gaps and remains behind F2 in attack direction; no implied possession transfer or owed return.

limitations: Advisory author; not reviewed, approved or applied.
No motion, reach, timing, gaze, collision or completed pass simulated.
Render/mobile legibility and U13 challenge require independent assessment.
Scene setup unchanged; proposed short movements are directions, not scored destinations.
Canonical carried-puck offset checked with makeScene; no rendered screenshot inspected by author.

geometry.units: metres; source x/y; angle in degrees
geometry.method: makeScene canonical owner-facing puck offset; Euclidean point-to-segment distances. One-metre trial positions are analysis examples only, not movement simulation or scored targets.
geometry.limits: Point clearance is not stick/body reach or interception feasibility; endpoint does not prove route safety.

imageDependency: Options require locating named players or rink landmarks relative to YOU; prompt does not supply those positions. Briefing supplies some context, so no claim that image is sole information source.
